#5095. Judge Acquits Brothers in $25 Million Ethereum MEV Case After Finding No Proven Wire Fraud

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

A Manhattan federal judge has acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno of criminal charges stemming from a 2023 Ethereum trading maneuver that prosecutors said extracted about $25 million. The decision is important, but the takeaway needs precision. It does not amount to judicial approval of every aggressive trading technique on public blockchains. Instead, the judge found that prosecutors failed to prove the material misrepresentations necessary for wire fraud and related convictions in this particular case.

The case concerned maximal extractable value, or MEV, the ability to affect the ordering or inclusion of blockchain transactions for financial gain. Prosecutors said the brothers engineered a bait-and-switch involving Ethereum validator infrastructure and trading bots in April 2023. Their alleged manipulation diverted value that the bots otherwise expected to capture. The defense contested the fraud theory. The unusual technical setting made the case a test of how existing criminal statutes apply to blockchain transactions that may be opportunistic or adversarial but do not necessarily resemble ordinary deceptive financial communications.

US District Judge Jessica Clarke focused on whether the conduct, as charged and proved, met the legal requirements for fraud. According to the ruling reported by Reuters and The Block, the relevant transactions did not involve material false representations of the kind prosecutors needed to establish. The judge distinguished that legal test from the question of whether the behavior was fair, ethical or objectionable. She also noted the absence of a regulated-market rule prohibiting the charged conduct in that setting. An acquittal under particular charges does not pronounce on every possible theory of liability.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Kava Lend collateral exploit.

The brothers were arrested in May 2024, and a jury failed to reach a verdict in November 2025. That sequence matters when interpreting Monday’s ruling: the result followed substantial litigation rather than a quick dismissal immediately after an indictment. The court’s reasoning offers a specific limit on a criminal fraud case, not a complete set of rules for MEV markets. Other facts, jurisdictions or statutory claims could produce different outcomes. Describing the ruling as the legalization of MEV attacks would overstate what the court decided.

MEV remains a practical concern for users who trade on-chain. Transaction ordering, block building and the design of trading bots can affect execution prices and who captures value. Better routing, slippage controls and protocol-level improvements may reduce some forms of extraction, but they do not eliminate competition over transaction priority. Legal certainty matters for developers and traders, while consumer protection remains a separate operational issue. The industry will be watching how prosecutors and policymakers respond to the limits the judge identified.

A ruling on criminal liability also leaves open the technical question of how MEV infrastructure should be designed. Relays, builders and validators can change their software or operational policies, but those changes have different trade-offs for permissionlessness, censorship resistance and execution fairness. Developers can study the facts of this case without treating the acquittal as a blanket endorsement of every form of transaction manipulation. The legal finding is narrower: the government did not prove the fraudulent representation required for the charged offences on the trial record.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Clearpool token-migration safeguards.

The headline is an acquittal in a closely watched federal case, not a blanket safe harbour for exploiting counterparties. For Ethereum users, it reinforces the need to distinguish legal allegations, proven misrepresentations and the technical safeguards available during on-chain execution.

Jensen Huang petition goes viral and Elon Musk joins 160,000 signers. Return odds doubled Sunday and Nvidia jumped 3%, then faded. Levels to watch.

Elon Musk said on Friday, November 13, that he is signing the Jensen Huang petition, an open letter asking Nvidia’s board to bring back its former chief executive. Huang resigned a day earlier, after reports of extramarital affairs.

By Monday, the “Stand with Jensen” letter had more than 160,000 signatures. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick have also backed it. The letter asks the board to reinstate Huang while an independent investigation establishes the facts.

A petition backing Huang has drawn 175,000 signatures.

Yet prediction markets give Huang just an 18%… pic.twitter.com/BZl5KheVnq

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 16, 2026

We matched Polymarket’s odds of Huang’s return with a 24/7 Nvidia stock contract on Hyperliquid. Musk’s post lifted the odds but barely moved the stock. A sharper jump in the odds on Sunday evening did: the stock rose 3% within two hours, then gave it all back by Monday.

So how is Nvidia’s stock reacting, one day before earnings?

Musk posted on X that “a petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too.” He had said earlier that hiring Huang would be “an honor.”

The petition is hosted at standwithjensen.com. Signers report their own job titles, and the site does not verify them. More than 7,500 say they work at the company, about 18% of its staff.

The company says it is choosing a search firm for the CEO role and has not formally approached any candidates. Chief financial officer Colette Kress runs the company in the meantime.

Nasdaq is shut on weekends, but the stock still trades around the clock as a perpetual contract, a futures-style contract with no expiry date, on Hyperliquid. Polymarket’s longer bets show how far the Jensen Huang petition still has to go. Traders give Huang a 37.5% chance of rejoining by the end of 2027, but only 5.6% by November 30.

On the daily chart, Hyperliquid’s NVDA contract trades at $156.93. It sits below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $199.26, and its 200-day EMA at $206.42. On Nasdaq, the shares closed Friday at $162.85, down 18.6% since November 4.

The Jensen Huang petition has moved the odds more than the stock. Musk’s backing barely shifted the price, and Sunday’s jump faded within a day. Tuesday’s earnings, the first under Kress, are likely to matter more to Nvidia shares than any petition.

#5092. US Supreme Court Turns Down Custodia Bank Appeal Over Federal Reserve Master Account

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Custodia Bank has reached the end of a significant route through the US federal courts in its effort to obtain direct access to Federal Reserve payment services. On November 16, the Supreme Court denied the Wyoming-chartered institution’s petition to review the dispute. The decision leaves a lower-court ruling in place. It is not a fresh opinion deciding every question about crypto-focused banks or an announcement that all such institutions must be kept out of the payments system.

Supreme Court docket 26-62 records a straightforward entry: the petition was denied on November 16, 2026. The justices did not agree to hear oral arguments and issue a merits opinion on the dispute. In practical terms, the lower-court position remains operative, but the denial should not be presented as the Supreme Court affirmatively endorsing each part of the earlier reasoning. This procedural distinction is important. It marks the end of this review attempt while leaving future policy and account-design questions to regulators, lawmakers and separate legal processes.

A Federal Reserve master account gives a qualified institution access to central-bank payment services without depending on another bank for the same connection. Custodia applied through the Kansas City Fed in 2020, arguing that its state bank charter supported its request. The application was denied in January 2023 following disputes over the institution’s business model and the risks the Fed identified. Custodia challenged the outcome, contending that federal law limited the Fed’s discretion. The appellate ruling instead recognised discretion to approve or deny applications in the relevant circumstances.

For related context, see our earlier report on Hong Kong's crypto licensing proposals.

The banking system is already debating whether some new financial firms should receive narrower forms of direct payments access. A proposed limited or “skinny” account would not necessarily provide the same services or rights as a full master account. That difference matters to institutions building business models around settlement speed, access costs and interest treatment. Even if a different account structure emerges, a future limited product should not be confused with the full access Custodia originally sought. The exact eligibility conditions and supervision requirements will determine whether such designs change the industry materially.

Crypto companies operating as banks or partnering with banks have a commercial interest in dependable dollar settlement, but charter status and payment-system access are not interchangeable. Firms may still use intermediary banking arrangements, with associated concentration and operational risks. The Custodia decision removes one possible path to overturn a prior denial; it does not prohibit new applications or resolve every question about emerging financial infrastructure. The next informative developments will be formal Fed rules, account approvals and the requirements attached to them.

The practical consequence for businesses is continuing uncertainty rather than an abrupt change to payment access. A firm can be licensed at the state level and still face a separate federal assessment of whether it may hold a Reserve Bank account. Policymakers who want to expand access must resolve supervision, settlement risk and eligibility in rules that Reserve Banks can actually apply. Meanwhile, fintech firms may keep using correspondent banks and other intermediaries, with the associated costs and dependencies those arrangements create.

For related context, see our earlier report on custody arrangements for a US bitcoin ETF.

The clearest fact is in the court record: review was denied. Whether the broader US payment system opens new pathways for digital-asset banks depends on future decisions, not on an expansive reading of this one-line order.

Reporting sources: US Supreme Court docket 26-62 · The Block chronology

Nvidia, IBM and Fermilab announced new tools for quantum error correction on Nov. 16, and the news comes amid a debate in the crypto industry about "Q-Day," the moment when a quantum computer will be able to break Bitcoin's cryptography. As of Monday, the price of Bitcoin stands at $64,580.

Nvidia released a new decoding algorithm, TCBP-JOBS, on Nov. 16. According to the company, the algorithm delivers up to 13,000x faster decoding compared with existing leading algorithms, and it cuts the computation time for researching new quantum computing designs from 12 weeks to 45 minutes.

Nvidia said that the algorithm helps researchers find designs that use physical qubits more efficiently, "shortening the path to practical fault-tolerant quantum computing."

Nvidia and IBM also announced plans for a modular quantum computing codesign platform with Fermilab. IBM and Nvidia are placing Nvidia DGX B200 systems next to IBM quantum computers, including those powered by IBM Quantum Nighthawk, and researchers will use the platform to develop and test error-correction codes.

"Making quantum computers useful for science requires advances in error correction, applications and the systems that bring quantum processors and accelerated computing together," said Krysta Svore, vice president of applied research for quantum computing at Nvidia.

A 2022 study by researchers from the University of Sussex estimated that breaking Bitcoin's encryption within a day would require around 13 million physical qubits.

IBM Quantum Nighthawk, which IBM calls its fastest quantum processor, has 120 qubits. According to Nvidia, errors in quantum processors "limit the complexity and duration of the computations they can perform."

In 2024, Bitcoin developer Hunter Beast proposed BIP-360, a new output type that would protect coins from quantum attacks. In July 2025, Casa co-founder Jameson Lopp also suggested a plan to phase out legacy signatures and move coins to quantum-resistant addresses.

Early coins mined by Satoshi Nakamoto sit on addresses with public keys that are already visible on the blockchain.

In November 2024, NIST proposed to stop allowing vulnerable public-key algorithms, including elliptic curve cryptography, after 2035.

#5089. Cardano Foundation Seeks Nearly 25 Million ADA for 2027 Events With Token Price Below Budget Assumption

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

A new Cardano community-treasury request raises an awkward budgeting question: what happens when an events programme is priced in dollars but funded in a volatile token? The Cardano Foundation has proposed withdrawing 24,995,775 ADA for a roughly $5 million global conference programme in 2027. Its calculation uses an ADA price of $0.20, while the token was trading nearer $0.15 during Tuesday’s reporting. The proposal is not approved spending, and the difference between those prices is substantial.

The proposed programme covers 12 conferences across multiple regions, with sponsorships, exhibition booths, project participation, travel and associated side events. The Foundation says participating Cardano teams would gain access to shared stands and opportunities to meet developers, partners and prospective users. Of the planned dollar budget, about $2 million relates to sponsorships, with additional material allocations for exhibition equipment, travel and hackathons. This is a marketing and ecosystem-development request to the community treasury, not an investment in a financial asset owned by token holders.

At the assumed price of 20 cents, the requested 24.995 million ADA represents just under $5 million. At 15 cents, the same number of tokens is worth roughly $3.75 million, leaving an indicative shortfall of about $1.25 million. The precise gap will change with the token price and timing of any withdrawal or conversion. The Foundation has indicated that it would operate within the amount actually withdrawn. Delegates therefore need to assess both the strategic case for the programme and how a variable funding base could change its scope.

For related context, see our earlier report on Cardano's Leios scaling development.

Cardano delegated representatives previously rejected funding for the Foundation’s 2026 flagship summit, which was later cancelled. The episode is relevant because governance votes can impose real spending discipline rather than serving as automatic approval for an established institution. The new request follows a separate treasury controversy over a proposal to purchase physical copper. These are distinct decisions, but both show delegates scrutinising what counts as worthwhile use of the community’s assets. A proposal document is not a guarantee that funds will be released.

Conference participation can build relationships and product awareness, yet measuring its return is harder than counting transactions or users. The Foundation has outlined targets for contacts, developer engagement and potential collaborations. Delegates can compare those targets with the cost per event and seek clear reporting on actual results. They can also evaluate whether unspent assets would return to the treasury and whether cost overruns could trigger new requests. The vote will test both confidence in the programme and tolerance for the gap between dollar estimates and ADA-denominated funding.

The debate is also a test of how decentralized treasury decisions are explained. Proposal authors should publish the ADA conversion rate, the dates on which it was calculated, a fiat-cost breakdown, milestone-based disbursements and a clear mechanism for returning unused funds. Voters can then compare expected community reach against alternative uses of scarce treasury assets. Without such measurement, even a successful event is hard to evaluate financially; with it, later proposals can cite more than attendance estimates or social-media impressions.

For related context, see our earlier report on a recent token-holder governance dispute.

This is a live governance choice, not a concluded allocation. The most useful follow-up will be the voting result, any adjusted programme budget and the Foundation’s eventual reporting against its participation targets—not a price forecast based on a single proposal.

#5088. Harvard Refuses to Dump Bitcoin Holdings Despite Downturn

Elite university Harvard maintains significant Bitcoin exposure as it holds over 3 million shares of a Bitcoin ETF, a recent regulatory filing has revealed.

Harvard University remains highly exposed to Bitcoin (BTC) as the elite institution continues to hold over 3 million shares of a Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF).

As per Bitcoin Magazine’s Nov. 16 report, Harvard Management Company, which manages Harvard University’s endowment, held 3,044,612 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

The Form 13F filing by Harvard University with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) showed that its investment in the Bitcoin ETF was worth roughly $144.1 million at the end of the third quarter.

Notably, Harvard did not change its Bitcoin ETF share count during the third quarter. The university held the same number of shares as reported at the end of June.

Harvard first disclosed its investment in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF during the second quarter of 2025.

As per Harvard's Form 13F filing submitted on Aug. 8, 2025, it held 1,906,000 IBIT shares at the end of the second quarter. The investment was worth roughly $116.7 million as of June 30.

The university subsequently increased its Bitcoin exposure significantly.

For instance, at the end of September 2025, Harvard held 6,813,612 IBIT shares, worth roughly $442.9 million. The Bitcoin ETF was the biggest investment that Harvard publicly reported at the time.

Later, however, the university started trimming its Bitcoin exposure. For example, during the fourth quarter of 2025, Harvard reduced its IBIT holdings by about 21.4%. Its total share holdings fell to 5.35 million.

During the first quarter of 2026, Harvard again reduced its Bitcoin exposure by 43.1%. This brought down the number of IBIT shares to roughly 3.04 million.

Since then, the university has maintained this number of shares. Harvard's quarter-end share count has remained unchanged in recent quarters.

Harvard University is not the only top-tier American university that has gained exposure to the biggest cryptocurrency by market capitalization.

In October 2024, Emory University became the first U.S. university endowment to publicly disclose its holdings in a Bitcoin ETF.

It held roughly 2.7 million shares of Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust, worth over $15 million at the time.

Meanwhile, in May 2025, Brown University disclosed its holdings of 105,000 shares of BlackRock's IBIT, worth roughly $4.9 million as of March 31 of that year.

Later, Brown doubled its stake, bringing its holdings to 212,500 shares.

Meanwhile, Dartmouth College has also joined the list of universities with exposure to cryptocurrency ETFs.

In its recent filing, Dartmouth College disclosed that it held 201,531 IBIT shares. The investment was worth roughly $9.5 million as of the end of September 2026.

Optimizely attack infects 178 websites, steals crypto and card data, and exposes users to wallet-address swaps and iPhone exploits.

An Optimizely attack on Monday, November 16, planted crypto-stealing code on the websites of 178 organizations, including Ledger, HSBC, Zoom, the BBC and CNN. The malicious script swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed card numbers, and tried to break into iPhones for about 19 hours before it was cleaned up.

BREAKING: A cyberattack hit 178 major organizations, including Zoom, CNN, BBC, Fox News, HSBC, Ledger, Equifax, Salesforce, IKEA and Air France-KLM, by loading malware on the Optimizely Web platform, exposing visitors to scripts built to steal payment data and exploit iOS…

— The Hormuz Letter (@HormuzLetter) November 17, 2026

Optimizely is a tool companies use to test different versions of their web pages. An attacker slipped code into the scripts it serves, so every site that loaded them ran the malware.

We traced the attacker’s Bitcoin wallet. It received five payments worth about $5,500, and one victim alone sent nearly 90% of it. Bitcoin barely moved while the attack ran.

So what happened, and what is the real impact of hacks like this one?

Security researcher Scott Helme of Report URI found the code and published a full breakdown. The attacker wrote it into a settings field in customers’ Optimizely projects, so it was served from Optimizely’s own servers and looked legitimate.

Optimizely said it “secured affected user accounts and added protections against further unauthorized code delivery.” Report URI found no sign that Ledger hardware wallets themselves were breached. The danger was on the website, where a copied address could be swapped before a user pasted it.

#5084. Solana Drops “Mainnet Beta” Label as Foundation Introduces Protocol Version 1.0

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Solana is retiring a label that has accompanied the blockchain since its launch: “mainnet beta.” In a November 16 announcement, the Solana Foundation introduced protocol version 1.0 and said the network should now be described simply as mainnet. It is a meaningful coordination change for developers and operators, but the Foundation was also explicit about what it is not. Users do not need to move funds, update token addresses or assume that a new feature has suddenly been enabled.

Solana has operated as a live production network for years while retaining the beta designation. Removing that wording is not a chain migration, hard reset or new issuance event. Accounts, SOL balances, applications and historical transactions remain on the same network, according to the Foundation. This matters for holders who may encounter posts suggesting they must claim a replacement token or connect a wallet to an upgrade portal. There is no such user requirement in the announcement. The change concerns how the live protocol is named and described.

The more technical development is a shared protocol version that is separate from the software version of any one validator client. Solana infrastructure includes Agave and Firedancer implementations, and those releases have their own numbering schemes. A network-level protocol number can make it clearer which clients support a given set of protocol rules, reducing reliance on one implementation as the reference point. That is coordination infrastructure rather than a substitute for testing. Validators still need to follow release notes and compatibility instructions for the specific software they deploy.

For related context, see our earlier report on recent Solana developer and validator updates.

A common protocol designation makes future network changes easier to communicate across independent implementations and tools. It could also help documentation, explorers and service providers describe compatibility consistently. But the Foundation cautioned that announcing a protocol version does not activate every associated improvement in one step. Feature activations and software rollouts retain their own schedules and technical requirements. Claims that Solana 1.0 instantly adds a particular throughput increase, fee mechanism or transaction feature should therefore be checked against separate activation notices.

For applications and RPC providers, the near-term work is keeping technical references current and watching client release guidance. For everyday users, the main practical change may simply be seeing “mainnet” rather than “mainnet beta” in wallets or interfaces. The market may attach symbolic significance to the milestone, but label changes are not a reliable stand-in for uptime, decentralisation, performance or adoption. Those outcomes still need to be measured independently as the network evolves.

Protocol labels are useful only if developers can connect them to concrete compatibility guarantees. Projects that integrate wallets, exchanges and payment systems still need to test RPC behavior, client changes and transaction-handling assumptions against real releases. Validators likewise need to monitor operator guidance instead of interpreting '1.0' as a permanent freeze in features or risk. A shared versioning convention may make upgrades easier to communicate, but sustained performance and reliable incident response remain the evidence users ultimately experience.

Solana 1.0 is best understood as a naming and versioning milestone. It establishes a common language for the protocol while leaving the hard work of shipping, activating and measuring future improvements to the network’s normal processes.

Reporting sources: Solana Foundation announcement

#5083. Ripple's Schwartz Reveals Why XRP Ledger Used Satoshi's Code

Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has shared the reason the XRP Ledger (XRPL) used code and cryptography from Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, in its early stages.

In his Nov. 16 post on X, Schwartz said they primarily chose to do so for security reasons and to prevent backlash from the Bitcoin community when the XRP Ledger was still in its early development.

The conversation started when prominent XRPL validator Vet (@Vet_X0) pointed out how some of Satoshi Nakamoto's initial design decisions are still present in the XRP Ledger's structure.

Vet said that the XRP Ledger initially used helper functions from the original Bitcoin software, including timekeeping functions coded by Satoshi Nakamoto himself.

Some of those helper functions were reportedly copied by Jed McCaleb, one of the early developers of the XRP Ledger. The original Bitcoin code even included a comment left by the mysterious creator of Bitcoin.

Afterward, Schwartz shared the reason why XRP Ledger developers opted to use the cryptographic options from Bitcoin instead of creating new ones.

"We did things that way in the very early days because we didn't want to be potentially facing criticism that our choices for those core crypto functions were less secure than Bitcoin's," said Schwartz.

In other words, XRP Ledger developers opted to use Bitcoin's cryptographic options to avoid possible controversial security-related decisions when creating a new cryptocurrency network.

Later on, Vet asked Schwartz if their decision helped gain acceptance among Bitcoin supporters who looked at their protocol in its early stages.

Schwartz said it was hard to say whether it helped or not.

"It's hard to say. Obviously we never got those criticisms. But it's hard to know if we would have," Schwartz said.

Additionally, the Ripple executive pointed out that it was uncertain whether the developers could have come up with better options if they had chosen to make their own cryptographic decisions.

"I'm not sure we would have come up with better ones had we made our own decisions anyway," Schwartz wrote.

It is worth noting that the original Bitcoin code copied in the early stages of the XRP Ledger is no longer present in the network's codebase.

According to Vet, the remaining parts of Satoshi Nakamoto's timekeeping code were deleted in December 2014 by former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis.

There are two crucial cryptographic design decisions from Bitcoin that are still used on the XRP Ledger.

#5082. Tokenized stocks are exactly where stablecoins were in 2020 – How?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Stablecoins started as a way to hold dollars on-chain. Then people started lending, trading, and earning with them. In time, DeFi grew up around them.

Tokenized stocks are heading down the same route now, and the resemblance is uncanny.

What’s worth noting here is how much of it is actually being used.

According to data from Token Terminal, tokenized stocks deposited into DeFi are now worth about $300 million. A year ago, that was at approx. $12.5 million.

This number didn’t move at all through late 2025. Things picked up in the spring, blasted through $100 million by around August, and then shot past a quarter million in September.

It’s also a bigger share of the market now. That $300 million is 6.3% of the $4.8 billion tokenized stock market cap. Last year, only 2.4% was being put to work.

Because once they’re there, holders can borrow against them, earn fees by providing liquidity, or chase yield.

And every new way to use them, is essentially one more reason not to cash out.

Tokenized stocks now have a market cap of about $4.8 billion. Stablecoins crossed that exact number in March 2020. Since then, stablecoins have grown, 59 times over! The number is at $285 billion now.

Tokenized stocks are moving fast too. They were worth only a few tens of millions in early 2025.

But why? A blockchain is basically a ledger for assets, and it gets more useful when it holds things people really want. U.S Stocks are about as in-demand as it gets.

Stablecoins didn’t get to where they are without the effort.

They made it through the COVID crash, the Terra collapse, FTX, and the USDC de-peg after SVB failed. Market cap fell by 28% between February 2022 and October 2023, then spiked up to a high by September 2024.

What kept them going though? Cash and T-bill reserves backed every token, plus people who actually wanted to use them.

Tokenized stocks follow the same 1:1 idea.

Except the risk factor is higher. So is the potential for gains.

#5080. Trezor Warns 27,000 Shipping Orders Were Exposed in Partner Breach, Not Wallet Keys

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Hardware-wallet maker Trezor has disclosed a breach at shipping partner Skladon affecting data connected with approximately 27,000 customer orders. The incident is serious because a delivery address and product purchase history can reveal who may own crypto. It is also important not to turn a data-exposure story into a false claim that customer wallets were drained. Trezor says its own systems were not compromised, and the disclosed records did not include wallet backups, PINs or passphrases.

Trezor says Skladon informed it on November 15 of unauthorized access linked to an incident on November 7. The data at issue concerned orders placed between August 9 and November 7, 2026. The company estimates roughly 27,000 affected orders and says the investigation is continuing. The records included names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses and information about orders and products bought. A limited number of earlier August customers may also have been affected even though their information had been anonymized within Trezor’s own systems before the notification process.

Someone with a buyer’s name, address and exact device order can craft a convincing phishing message or impersonate customer support. The same combination may create physical-security concerns if a criminal believes the household controls valuable assets. None of this requires compromising the hardware wallet’s cryptographic security. Trezor says it never requests wallet recovery data by telephone and warns affected users to treat unexpected calls, texts, emails and letters with suspicion. If a message uses authentic order details, that does not make its instructions legitimate.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Unocoin wallet-key incident.

The company says it has contacted affected customers it can still reach and notified a data-protection authority. It is introducing or expanding anonymous pickup at collection points in much of Europe, reducing the amount of residential delivery information involved in future orders. Trezor also says it is working to shorten customer-data retention from 90 to 45 days, with further reductions under consideration. Those steps address the long-term exposure of operational records rather than claiming that a damaged secret key can be repaired after the fact.

Customers should go directly to the vendor’s known website for official support rather than follow contact details supplied in an unsolicited message. They should never type a recovery phrase into a web form or share it with a caller. Buyers can also consider whether their delivery address and household security require extra attention. Anyone receiving threats should contact appropriate local authorities. The precise number of affected people, rather than orders, may differ, and the final breach scope may change as investigators establish what was exported.

A legitimate package or delivery notice is especially convincing because it can refer to a real order. Criminals might use the information for emails, texts, calls or fraudulent web pages that look like shipping support. Wallet owners should be wary of any message that asks them to type a recovery phrase, install a replacement wallet application or approve an unexpected transaction. Those requests are unrelated to normal delivery updates. The strongest precaution is to verify a message through a separately opened official website, not by following a link in the message itself.

For related context, see our earlier report on Coinbase's discussion of cold-storage controls.

Reporting sources: Trezor official incident report

South Korean financial app Toss is preparing a built-in wallet that could make sending cryptocurrencies feel more like using an ordinary payments contact list. Local reports cited by crypto.news say the first release will support ether, Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC on Ethereum, with a rollout planned for the week of November 16. The platform has roughly 30 million registered users, though that figure must not be confused with 30 million wallet customers or a prediction of adoption.

The proposed Toss Coin Wallet would appear within the Assets area of the company’s established app. Users would be able to create a wallet, view balances, deposit supported assets and make transfers without first downloading a separate crypto-specific product. Reports describe contact-based sending that reduces the need to copy long addresses manually. That interface convenience does not change the underlying Ethereum transfer: moving ETH or stablecoins remains an on-chain operation, with network fees and irreversible settlement characteristics. The feature’s actual adoption will depend on customer onboarding and reliable day-to-day use, not simply the size of Toss’s existing registration base.

Toss has characterized the wallet as noncustodial, meaning it will not hold the assets on the customer’s behalf as an exchange typically would. The practical details of key management, recovery and account safeguards will therefore be important to examine once the product is live. Transactions will still require Ethereum gas payments even if Toss does not levy a separate platform transfer fee. Users also need to understand that a token sent to the wrong network or incompatible address can be hard or impossible to recover. A simplified contact screen should be evaluated alongside the security controls beneath it.

For related context, see our earlier report on stablecoin-supply and liquidity trends.

The initial version described in reporting is about holding and transferring three digital assets. It is not an announced exchange for buying crypto with Korean won, nor a completed stablecoin checkout integration across Toss merchants. The distinction matters because mobile finance applications can offer very different forms of crypto access, from payment rails to brokerage services. Toss has separately explored stablecoin payments and other blockchain infrastructure with partners, but exploratory pilots should not be counted as services already available to all customers.

South Korea’s policy discussion on domestically issued won-backed stablecoins is still developing. The Toss wallet’s initial lineup instead uses ether and existing dollar-pegged stablecoins. For regulators, the questions will include consumer disclosures, anti-money-laundering compliance and who is responsible when a user needs assistance. For competitors, the more immediate test is whether ordinary financial apps can make self-custody accessible without creating confusion over fees, network selection and support. Watch the live release notes rather than assuming every previously discussed partnership has launched together.

The important commercial questions concern the exact custody and onboarding model, not simply the size of Toss's existing customer base. A noncustodial wallet can bring new users on-chain, but those users still need access to funds, recovery tools, regulatory disclosures and reliable transaction support. USDT and USDC are dollar-linked assets with issuer and banking dependencies. If the product is launched as described, its adoption will be measured more usefully in funded wallets and sustained activity than in the total count of people who use the broader finance app.

If Toss delivers the described experience, it would be a distribution experiment for stablecoins on a major consumer platform. The sensible comparison is not registered app users versus crypto traders but activated wallets, successfully completed transfers and the controls offered when something goes wrong.

The crypto market remains under pressure, with Bitcoin dropping to a four-month low around $62,000 on November 15. SHIB, SOL and XLM all printed new lows on November 14, yet selling volume stayed well below earlier spikes, and oversold RSI readings suggest a recovery could be near, even though fundamental catalysts are still missing.

Thankfully, Shiba Inu's bearish rally might be fading sooner rather than later. The price's most recent red candle wasn't followed by a surge in selling volume, which could hint at a potential reversal.

On November 14, a single daily candle took SHIB below the July bottom around $0.0000041, with the wick reaching $0.0000037. At press time, the asset is trading at $0.00000387, the lowest level on the chart since March. Selling volume that day stayed well below the late July and August spikes.

Usually, when the price hits the bottom like that, the point of previously growing demand might become a source of additional selling pressure. For SHIB, it's the July zone, where buyers stepped in last time.

If we dive inside the 4HR price chart, we can clearly see a price/volume divergence, which is a good sign for bulls. Moving averages are diverging, so a quick retrace isn't yet possible. SHIB is trading below all of its moving averages, with the 200 EMA hanging at around $0.0000054. Bitcoin's drop to a four-month low around $62,000 on November 15 didn't help either.

Despite the death cross on the chart solidifying, there's a good chance it's not critical. The price is showing negative performance one way or another, but it's not going to add more fuel to the bearish furnace.

The cross formed near $96, where a shorter moving average dropped below the 200 EMA, and another moving average is about to follow. SOL is trading at $71.70 after a wick to around $67.50 on November 14. Since its late September peak near $125, Solana has lost over 40% of its value.

First of all, death crosses aren't as scary as they used to be. Second, the signal is inherently lagging, so it only reflects what was already priced in. It's more of a guideline for those who are looking for an entry.

The price is already oversold, but the bottom might be closer to $62, which is also reinforced by RSI. Back in June, $62 was the point where SOL bottomed out before the summer recovery.

Stellar has reached a potential price bottom where it might finally find ground for a retrace. The volume is relatively low, but the main issue is the lack of foundational recovery fuel.

XLM is trading at $0.1384 after dropping to $0.13 on November 14. That's below the May low around $0.142, the zone from which XLM spiked toward $0.30 in June. The RSI dipped below 30 during the drop. Short-term moving averages are crossing longer-term moving averages, and the issue here is that it's a signal of short-term aggravation. All of them are now above the price, with the 200 EMA at around $0.184.

The key here is the crypto market recovery in general.

A new connection between the Solflare wallet and MoneyGram Ramps aims to solve a practical stablecoin problem: a user can hold digital dollars on Solana but still need physical cash. MoneyGram says eligible Solflare users can now withdraw USDC as local currency at participating agent locations in more than 170 countries and territories. That geographic coverage is substantial, but it should not be read as an unconditional cash-out guarantee in every location or for every customer.

According to MoneyGram’s November 16 announcement, a Solflare user selects Withdraw, chooses MoneyGram, enters an amount of USDC and follows the guided payout process before collecting cash from a participating outlet. The integration links a self-custody wallet to a familiar physical distribution network. There is still a distinction between initiating a blockchain transfer and receiving funds at the counter: identity verification, local availability and payout requirements can affect completion. Users should rely on the official flow for quotes, instructions and confirmation rather than sending tokens to an address received in an unsolicited message.

MoneyGram is promoting zero cash-out fees for eligible Solflare users through December 31, 2026. That is a time-limited offer, not a permanent commitment that every step of a stablecoin withdrawal will be free of all possible costs. Network charges, exchange-rate effects or local requirements may be relevant to a particular transaction, and the published terms and quote should control. The ability to convert tokens into spendable local currency is likely to matter more to many users than a headline about blockchain throughput alone.

For related context, see our earlier report on the latest stablecoin-liquidity developments.

Stablecoins move value across digital networks, but they are not universally accepted as a way to pay everyday expenses. MoneyGram’s retail footprint provides a bridge for customers who need banknotes or a locally familiar cash service. The company says its Ramps business has grown substantially and is now being integrated with additional wallets. This arrangement could help cross-border recipients, freelancers or travelers, although actual savings compared with traditional remittance routes will vary by jurisdiction, payment size and the available alternatives.

Solflare users retain control of assets in their wallets before initiating a withdrawal, but redeeming those assets involves a service provider and its compliance procedures. That division should be explained clearly to avoid suggesting that a physical cash payout happens without intermediaries. MoneyGram is responsible for relevant payout operations, while the wallet provides access to the flow. The network’s permissionless transfer capabilities and the retail service’s regulated customer requirements are separate parts of the experience. Product reliability will be measured by the success rate of that handoff.

Coverage in a country does not guarantee that every local counter offers the same payout currency, opening hours or amount limits. A traveller should confirm eligibility, identification rules, transaction size, charges and whether the specific location participates before sending any digital asset. Unlike a regular card or bank withdrawal, an on-chain transfer can be irreversible even if a cash pickup is delayed. Clear status messages, refund procedures and support channels will therefore be as important to the product's reputation as the geographical scope of the partner network.

For related context, see our earlier report on a tokenized settlement trial by central banks.

The launch is a concrete use case for dollar stablecoins rather than a broad forecast about adoption. Its significance will depend on where customers can actually collect cash, the all-in cost after promotions end and whether the service remains dependable during high demand.

Reporting sources: MoneyGram launch announcement

#5073. Mastercard Spotlights XRP Ledger After Groundbreaking Test

After an important hackathon that demonstrated how AI agents could autonomously perform payments using blockchain, global payments giant Mastercard has spotlighted the XRP Ledger (XRPL).

36 hours. 179 hackers. 70 submissions. At the XRP Ledger Hackathon, developers used Mastercard Agent Pay for machines to explore new possibilities for micropayments and autonomous commerce, including how AI agents can transact within defined spending limits and with verified merchants. See what we learned about the future of agentic commerce: https://t.co/S4NwQxxuRi #AgenticCommerce #DigitalAssets #AI

Global payments giant Mastercard recently posted on X about the outcome of the XRP Ledger Hackathon. In the post, the payments firm detailed that 179 developers submitted 70 projects during the 36-hour event in Manhattan.

The focus of the competition was how to enable AI-powered agents to autonomously execute transactions and micropayments, engage with verified merchants and so forth, all while operating within budgets set by developers.

The hackathon was held as part of the preparations for Ripple’s annual conference called Swell. Mastercard, Amazon Web Services, QuickNode and Ledger supported the event, which had a prize pool of over $40,000.

Mastercard published an official article in which it mentioned the challenge given to developers. They had to build AI agents that could autonomously make payments to verified merchants without human input.

Also, the agents had to operate within a specified budget. They had to settle payments using Ripple’s USD-backed stablecoin called RLUSD. They had to do this on the XRP Ledger.

One of the purposes of the challenge was to showcase how blockchain infrastructure can enable micropayments. This is especially the case for micropayments smaller than one cent.

In the future, these micropayments could be valuable as AI agents start buying computational resources or requesting data from other AI agents and then making payments themselves for digital services.

Mastercard’s vice president of digital assets, Michael Broderick, stressed that the company's technology called Agent Pay for Machines could enable such payments.

One of the most interesting things mentioned in the Mastercard report might be how the XRP Ledger is increasingly being used for payments by machines.

Mastercard mentioned that over 500,000 transactions are being conducted daily on the XRPL by AI agents.

Also, it’s reported that Ripple has recorded over 10 million payments using the x402 internet payment protocol on XRPL. This comes less than three months after the protocol crossed the 1 million payment milestone on the network.

Chat Wars is a traditional role-playing game that is built around fantasy world-building, heroes, guilds, resources, and strategic decisions. Players start by building their characters and can collect resources, improve equipment, participate in activities, and contribute to their guild.

Combat, crafting, and resource management are all part of the game’s overall experience, so players can become part of a larger experience rather than just collecting points. Guild participation is a major part of the game, and groups can cooperate, coordinate, and work towards shared objectives.

Catizen lets users develop, combine, and manage digital cats. The main objective of the game is to collect new cats, merge similar ones, expand facilities, complete missions, and grow. Players can collect rewards, unlock new buildings, and participate in seasonal events.

The game has a more holistic approach than many other tap-to-earn games as it focuses on community interactions and long-term engagement. The game has evolved over time into an ecosystem of its own with a native token called CATI.

A very popular game in the space, Hamster Kombat also has a tap-to-earn format where the original gameplay revolved around managing a virtual crypto exchange owned by a CEO who was a hamster. PlayDeck has a large collection of casual games in a single Telegram Mini App, making it convenient for players who enjoy playing in new genres. It gives players a chance to explore challenges, puzzles, and reaction-based games.

MemeFi is a tap-to-earn combat game where players fight meme-inspired bosses, earn crypto rewards, and make character progressions. The main USP of the game is its combat, where players go up against enemies and defeat challenging opponents.

Users can also create various clans, manage their energy levels, or use boosters. MEMEFI is the utility and governance token of the platform and has a total supply of 10 billion.

Rocky Rabbit is a tap-to-earn mini-game that was built on the TON network. Players need to train their rabbits in the game, participate in duels and complete any tasks to rank higher. The game takes its inspiration from fitness and boxing.

The platform’s native token RBTC (RabBitcoin) was launched on TON in 2024, and players can join competitions and battles, earn rewards, and bonuses for referrals.

A famous retro-style pixel mini-game on TON, Yescoin lets users swipe their fingers across the screen to catch falling coins similar to Fruit Ninja. Players can complete missions, collect coins, upgrade their skills, and be a part of the community.

Players can buy upgrades and power-ups to boost their earnings, as it is managed by an energy system that regenerates over time. There are quests, missions, events, and various other options for players to earn rewards throughout the game.

A play-to-earn mini-game built around the Minesweeper mechanics that mixes it with dungeon exploration. Players need to explore a 5×5 grid where they tap blocks one by one and earn gold. If they choose the block that has a trap, the game is over.

Pixel Tap is a cyberpunk combat-themed mini-game where players can tap the screen to earn in-game coins, upgrade robot fighters, and take part in real-time battles against each other. It is part of the wider Pixelverse ecosystem, and the game revolves around tapping mechanics and PvP battles.

In-game currency can be earned through referrals, daily tasks, battles, and general activity. Players can get into battles and earn points and tokens in PvE and PvP settings. $PIXFI is the native token of the platform, and rewards can be earned in it.

Egg Drop is a play-to-earn game on the BNB Chain where players drop virtual eggs into target zones and score points while collecting points and levelling up “Birdies”. The eggs fall under various categories, such as white, yellow, royal, energy, punch, shield, attack, and steal types.

Accessibility and engagement are important parts of the game where the sessions are short and easy to navigate and aimed at users looking for time-intensive games. Token incentives and collected items can be accumulated through regular activity in the game.

Players can earn the token through the play-to-earn model and also by taking part in airdrops and boss raids. There are community events that help players interact with each other as well.

Telegram games give an easy and convenient way for players to engage with a lot of these tap-to-earn apps. They started out as simple games and have evolved into much more complex ecosystems of their own overtime, offering a wide variety of gaming experience.

Each game brings something different and can be appealing to a different type of gamer. However, it is advisable to do your own reseach before monetarily investing in any game.

#5071. CoW Swap Adds Native Solana Trading With Solver Auctions and a One-Year Volume-Fee Waiver

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

CoW Swap has launched an alpha that allows traders to start and finish asset swaps on Solana, extending an intent-based model previously associated with Ethereum. The basic difference is worth understanding: rather than manually choosing a route and submitting a conventional swap, users sign an instruction that competing solvers try to execute at acceptable terms. CoW DAO is also waiving its own volume fee on Solana for at least a year, a decision that should not be mistaken for the disappearance of all trading costs.

Before this release, CoW Swap could facilitate certain routes into Solana from Ethereum-compatible networks. The new alpha supports trades whose starting and ending assets are on Solana itself. That is a different proposition for applications already serving Solana users. The launch includes an integration with lending platform Kamino and access to a solver network that CoW DAO describes as comprising more than 30 participants. The alpha designation also matters: traders should check supported assets, order conditions and current operational limitations before assuming every feature available on other chains is identical.

With an intent-based order, a trader specifies the assets and the price or conditions they will accept. Solvers can compete to find a matching trade or route liquidity through available venues. CoW Swap says its batching and execution design can help reduce opportunities for certain sandwich attacks and avoid some failed on-chain swaps. That is a design objective, not a guarantee that every order will fill at the best imaginable price. Market depth, slippage, solver incentives and latency still shape outcomes, especially for thinly traded tokens.

For related context, see our earlier report on Solana confidentiality infrastructure.

CoW DAO says it will waive its own Solana volume fee for at least the first 12 months. Users should distinguish that platform charge from the economic costs of crossing bid-ask spreads, securing liquidity and potentially using network resources. Sponsored transactions can also change who pays an upfront network fee without making trade execution economically costless. The order’s displayed execution price and the eventual tokens received remain the meaningful comparison with other venues. Fee promotions are useful, but not a substitute for checking route quality.

Solana already has active trading infrastructure, so the question is not whether CoW Swap brings decentralized exchanges to a previously empty market. It is whether solver competition and order batching create a sufficiently different experience to attract liquidity and integrations. For lending applications, a reliable swap path can also affect liquidation and portfolio-management workflows. Independent measurements of fills, failed attempts, spreads and protection against adverse ordering will be more persuasive than the cumulative trade-volume figures of the protocol’s older networks.

Execution quality needs independent measurement. Users comparing an intent-based solver with a traditional aggregator should examine the final amount received after all network and protocol costs, the time needed to settle and how failed or partially filled routes are handled. The headline fee waiver should not obscure transaction costs or liquidity-provider economics that may still apply. Solana's faster settlement can improve the experience, but it does not by itself guarantee that every swap will beat a direct exchange quote under volatile market conditions.

For related context, see our earlier report on a recent DeFi market-security case.

The launch adds another execution model to Solana, not a guarantee against losses or manipulation. Users should treat an alpha product’s safeguards and fee arrangements as claims to verify through its documentation and trading results as adoption grows.

#5070. CFTC Makes Historic Move With Blockchain Derivatives Approval

The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has opened historic doors for blockchain technology adoption in traditional financial markets as it approves exchange and clearinghouse applications for blockchain-based derivatives market infrastructure.

On Nov. 16, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig announced that the commission had given the green light to exchange (designated contract market or DCM) and clearinghouse (derivatives clearing organization or DCO) applications for a company using blockchain technology for the execution and settlement of derivatives contracts.

As per the official statement, Selig considers this a major step forward for U.S. financial markets. He said that blockchain-based market infrastructure is compatible with current U.S. financial regulations.

"This approval makes clear that there is a regulatory path for companies that want to innovate and use blockchain technology to modernize how derivatives are traded and settled,"  he elaborated.

Selig pointed out that the U.S. derivatives markets have seen a number of technological advancements, from physical trading floors to electronic trading platforms.

Now, with blockchain technology, he believes there is an opportunity to further modernize financial market infrastructure without losing regulatory oversight and investor protections.

Notably, there is no technical architecture requirement imposed on derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses under the CFTC's current regulatory framework.

Therefore, firms that leverage blockchain-based networks can apply for regulatory approval under the same set of rules and regulations that apply to traditional financial market participants.

However, Selig also clarified that blockchain adoption is not a license to escape regulatory oversight.

Companies will still need to comply with rules covering anti-money laundering (AML), client protections, market monitoring, risk mitigation and other measures designed to protect the integrity of financial markets.

Simply put, the CFTC is looking to bring blockchain technology into regulated derivatives market infrastructure while maintaining the same standards as traditional financial market participants.

For some time, the CFTC chairman has been pushing for a scenario where U.S. companies developing emerging financial technologies can operate in the country without having to look to international markets.

The latest developments further reinforce the message that the U.S. is open for business for companies building blockchain-based financial market infrastructure, according to Selig.

In its report, the perpetual futures exchange said its Security Council returned about 5 million USDC to the affected trader. Interestingly, deposits and withdrawals were “back to normal” after the council switched off Guardian mode.

The exchange traced the leak to unofficial signing software and said its protocol and smart contracts were, fortunately enough, unaffected.

Lighter said it had paused withdrawals through Guardian mode. That basically allowed its Security Council to return around 5 million USDC.

The exchange said it was also working to recover funds linked to “an additional withdrawal attempt by the attacker.” However, a separate withdrawal of 10.39 million USDC had already gone through on Ethereum [ETH] before the pause was announced. Bubblemaps later traced some of those funds to Hyperliquid [HYPE].

Kevin Wang, a former market maker at Lighter, also weighed in on the incident. He wrote,

Lighter said it now required a wallet signature to move funds into public pools.

At the time of writing, Lighter [LIT] traded near $3, about 8% above its pre-incident range of $2.77–$2.78. LIT had rebounded about 29% from a brief wick near $2.33.

The rebound had already stalled near $3.07 on the hourly chart. An hourly close above that level would extend the recovery.

With LIT recovering, the dollar value of assets held on Lighter did not react the same way. On the 17th of November 2026, DeFiLlama showed Total Value Locked (TVL) of $671.04 million. That was down about 14% from $777.33 million before the incident.

Of course, derivatives activity also cooled around the incident. On the 16th of November, Open Interest fell 9% to $559.99 million, leaving less value in outstanding positions. Daily Perp Volume dropped 15% to $3.147 billion, showing fewer dollars traded in perpetual futures.

#5068. Bitwise Maps Solana to $80, $385 or $1,100 by 2031 in Scenario-Based Research

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Bitwise has published a five-year framework for Solana that includes very different possible outcomes for SOL’s price. The range extends from an $80 bear case to a $385 base case and an $1,100 bullish scenario for 2031, according to reporting on its November 16 research. Those numbers are scenarios, not an announcement that the token will reach any particular level. The interesting story is the set of expectations about tokenized securities, payments and on-chain trading required to justify the more ambitious outcome.

Bitwise’s paper, “Tokenization, 24/7 Trading, and the Economics of Solana,” links possible SOL valuations to the role a fast blockchain might play in financial activity. The firm argues that tokenized assets, payments and round-the-clock trading could shift more transactions on-chain over time. Its publicly available summary identifies a $385 base-case outlook for 2031. That is a modeled result within a research framework, not a quoted future market price or a probability-weighted consensus. Investors should read the full assumptions and risk disclosures before comparing the figure with spot trading.

The $1,100 scenario discussed in The Block’s coverage assumes a much larger tokenized-equity market and unusually strong Solana participation. Among the assumptions cited are a 5% tokenization of global stocks and a large share of resulting trading volume flowing through Solana. A scenario built on that scale can help illustrate upside sensitivity, but it also magnifies execution risk. There is no guarantee that securities issuers will tokenize at the modeled pace, or that Solana rather than other blockchains and traditional infrastructure will win most of the business.

For related context, see our earlier report on Solana treasury and staking disclosures.

Even if tokenized assets and payments grow, their relationship to the native token’s value depends on fee structures, network demand, supply dynamics and competition. Low transaction fees can attract activity without making each additional transaction economically equivalent to a large increase in token demand. Layer-two systems, private networks and alternative settlement solutions may also compete for institutional transactions. The mechanism from network activity to investment return needs to be assessed, not assumed. Forecast tables tend to look precise even when the underlying business model is uncertain.

The three cases are most useful as a way to frame questions: how much tokenized volume might actually migrate, how quickly payments grow, what share Solana can secure and how much capacity it would need. The bearish case also reminds readers that technological adoption and investor returns can diverge. Bitwise itself sells crypto investment products, so its commercial perspective should be noted while examining the research. Treat each figure as conditional on the inputs rather than as investment advice or an independent valuation fact.

Scenario analysis becomes more informative when its inputs are varied, rather than when the highest output is presented as a prediction. An investor could test a slower tokenization rollout, tighter fee competition, different staking rewards or a valuation multiple below the research base case. Small changes in several assumptions can compound over five years. Bitwise's work is useful as a model of how network activity might translate into token economics, but competing networks, policy choices and unforeseen technology changes could make realised outcomes very different.

Forecasts make headlines, but assumptions are where the debate belongs. Tracking tokenized equity usage, payment volumes, transaction economics and competition over the next five years will show whether the underlying thesis is getting stronger or weaker.

Reporting sources: Bitwise research introduction · The Block discussion of the scenarios

Malicious JavaScript code snippets were planted on the websites of 178 organizations.

The exploit originated inside Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform, a tool that many large companies use for A/B testing, which means showing users multiple versions of a page to determine which one is more effective.

Report URI estimates that on November 16 the code sat in 188 of the 1,611 Optimizely snippets it crawled, and the real number is most likely higher.

Among the websites that could become victims of the hack are some of the largest names in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Fox News, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock. BleepingComputer confirms that the script loads on many of them.

Essentially, the script's goal was to swap a wallet address on the page for the attacker's one, capture card numbers, take screenshots of pages and more. It was a whole stack of tools used to steal personal data, wallets and other assets.

According to Report URI, the attacker's wallets received about $7,040 within the first nine hours. That is a drop in the ocean considering the names involved, though the losses from card skimming are unknown. A card skimmer was added later that day, and a hidden iframe tried to load an iOS exploit chain on older iPhones.

Optimizely confirmed that an unauthorized party had exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation to add malicious JavaScript to certain customer projects. How the flaw worked is yet to be confirmed.

If successful, it could become one of the largest supply-chain attacks we have ever witnessed. Considering the attack came from a third party, we might see one of the largest service migrations in the world, as none of the third-party services and libraries can be trusted nowadays if used through an API.

Cryptocurrency services delegate certain tasks to third-party providers all the time, so witnessing a similar situation in our field is more than a possibility.

For product owners: stay cautious and rethink the use of services prone to exploits. For users: stay vigilant and try not to put all your eggs in one basket.

#5065. Elon Musk Joins 160,000 Backing Petition to Bring Jensen Huang Back to Nvidia

Elon Musk Joins 160,000 Backing Petition to Bring Jensen Huang Back to Nvidia

Elon Musk has thrown his support behind a campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO, as the ousted chipmaker co-founder reportedly weighs a comeback just days after resigning.

"A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too," the Tesla and SpaceX CEO tweeted on Friday. Musk had previously said it would be "an honor" to hire Huang.

A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 13, 2026

The "Stand with Jensen" open letter calls on Nvidia's board to bring Huang back while an independent investigation establishes the facts. It has drawn more than 160,000 signatures, including Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, CNBC reported, though the site notes that signatories' affiliations are self-reported and unverified. More than 7,500 signatories identified themselves as Nvidia employees, The Guardian reported, a figure it said was equivalent to 18% of the company's workforce.

The campaign follows internal calls from Nvidia staff for Huang's return.

Huang has discussed the possibility of returning with confidants, the Financial Times reported, citing multiple people familiar with the matter. One ally told the newspaper they were assembling a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his reinstatement and would seek support from the White House, adding that the effort had Huang's backing.

Even supporters acknowledged the obstacles. "Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offence," one person involved in the effort told the FT.

Two major Nvidia shareholders, Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management's Gavin Baker, urged the board in an open letter on Friday to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang."

Huang resigned as Nvidia's president, CEO and board member on Thursday, capping a week of reports of affairs with Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom U.S. officials suspect of spying for China, and with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO.

The campaign faces resistance in Washington. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Nvidia should look outside the company for its next CEO. "They need a dramatic shake-up," he told Fox News.

Bessent said on Sunday Morning Futures that questions over Nvidia's compliance with U.S. export restrictions were the bigger issue, and that the company should be judged on whether it had "intentionally ignored the warning signs" of shell companies in Singapore. He said he wanted answers "in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel." Huang also faces congressional inquiries into Nvidia's chip exports to China, as well as a proposed shareholder class action.

Nvidia's board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor, the FT has reported. "We are in the process of selecting a search firm for the NVIDIA CEO role. We have not formally engaged any potential candidates," an Nvidia spokesperson told CNBC.

Analysts are divided on Huang's chances. "We see no chance Jensen comes back to Nvidia as CEO," Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. said in a note cited by CNBC, while Seaport Research Partners' Jay Goldberg said Huang could stage "a second act" if he gets through his legal troubles. Former White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci was blunter: "The FBI doesn't take petitions," he tweeted.

Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on Tuesday, the first under Kress.

#5064. Safe wallet reportedly loses $6.5M as Zodiac suspects key compromise

Zodiac’s co-founder said a likely compromised key and overly permissive wallet settings enabled the theft, rather than a flaw in its smart contracts.

A Safe wallet reportedly lost about $6.45 million in cryptocurrency Monday, with Zodiac’s co-founder pointing to a likely compromised key and the wallet’s permissions settings rather than a flaw in Zodiac’s contracts.

Blockchain security firm PeckShield reported the suspected theft, citing onchain investigator Specter. Ethereum blockchain records reviewed by Cointelegraph show that approximately 4.39 million USDC (USDC) and 1.72 million syrupUSDC tokens were transferred from the wallet in a single transaction on Monday.

Johannes Moormann, co-founder of Zodiac, told Cointelegraph that his team reviewed the transaction and confirmed it passed through the wallet’s Zodiac Roles Modifier, which checked the transfer against its configured permissions policy and allowed it. “There is no vulnerability in the module. The contracts worked correctly. The transaction came from the key of a long-standing role member, which was most likely compromised,” he said.

Moormann added that the wallet’s custom permissions policy permitted the transaction, almost certainly unintentionally. He said the wallet’s operators controlled its keys and permissions, and that Zodiac had neither access to them nor involvement in the setup. Zodiac has not been in contact with the affected team.

Specter first flagged the Zodiac Roles module as part of the suspected attack. PeckShield also said the attacker used approximately $813,000 to purchase Monero-linked tokens on Hyperliquid.

The Zodiac Roles module allows Safe users to assign permissions for specific transactions. Moormann said the incident did not indicate a vulnerability affecting other wallets using the module.

The identity of the wallet owner has not been established. Cointelegraph contacted Safe and Gnosis Guild for comment but had not received a response by publication.

Related: DOJ moves to seize $1.2B from Binance hack, disrupts FaceStealer scam

Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery traced funds from the Safe wallet through multiple addresses to Hyperliquid, where five accounts purchased approximately $1 million in XMR1 tokens.

The firm noted similarities with fund movements following Monday’s Lighter incident, including a 160 Ether (ETH) transfer and purchases of XMR1.

However, Bitquery said it found no transfers connecting the two wallet groups and could not establish whether the same actor was involved.

#5063. Strategy Adds 485 Bitcoin as It Repurchases $228 Million of STRC Preferred Shares

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Strategy has added 485 Bitcoin to its already enormous treasury, but its November 16 disclosure carries another figure that deserves equal attention: the company also repurchased about $228 million of STRC preferred shares. The update is a reminder that digital-asset treasury companies make capital-allocation decisions across both their crypto holdings and the securities used to finance them. Counting BTC alone cannot tell investors whether each step improves their economic position.

Strategy says it bought 485 BTC between November 9 and November 15 for approximately $33.4 million, at an average acquisition price of about $68,887 per coin. The purchase raised aggregate holdings to 850,849 BTC. The company reported an aggregate acquisition cost of around $64.2 billion, equivalent to roughly $75,452 for each Bitcoin held across its history. Those cost figures are not the current market value of the treasury, and the average changes when additional purchases are made. The purchase window also matters because it spans a period of falling Bitcoin prices rather than a single quoted trade.

STRC is part of Strategy’s preferred-capital structure. The company has used such instruments alongside equity and other financing tools to build and manage its balance sheet. Buying back preferred shares below their stated amount can affect obligations, market confidence and the securities still outstanding. It also uses capital that could otherwise serve different purposes. Investors therefore need to compare the BTC acquisition with the repurchase, cash reserves and dividend commitments. Describing the update as an unqualified large Bitcoin bet overlooks the simultaneous management of financing instruments.

For related context, see our earlier report on Twenty One Capital's bitcoin treasury results.

Strategy’s treasury size is a headline measure of exposure, but a common shareholder owns an interest in a company with other securities and obligations ahead of ordinary equity. Increases in BTC can coexist with changes in share count, leverage, dividend requirements and the value of preferred securities. Simple “Bitcoin per company” comparisons do not measure everything shareholders receive. The company provides additional proprietary metrics intended to describe its strategy, but it warns that these are not identical to profitability or conventional balance-sheet valuations.

Bitcoin’s November decline puts the resilience of capital structures under greater scrutiny. A company can keep buying assets while still facing pressure if its shares, preferred securities or access to funding weaken. The key disclosures to monitor are future BTC purchases, security repurchases, cash and liquid reserves, and any changes in capital-raising conditions. The latest acquisition is independently meaningful, but its significance for investors depends on the full balance sheet and the prices at which capital is issued and retired.

Capital structure deserves particular attention because Strategy finances parts of its Bitcoin accumulation through instruments with distinct investor claims. Preferred shares, common equity and debt can behave differently during sharp BTC drawdowns, especially when market prices diverge from accounting values. The relevant questions are not just how many coins were bought but what resources funded the transaction, which obligations were reduced and what exposure remained per common share. Investors should consult the full financing disclosures rather than treating a gross BTC increase as automatic shareholder accretion.

For related context, see our earlier report on JPMorgan's Strategy shareholdings disclosure.

The company has clearly continued acquiring Bitcoin through weakness. The more complete story is that its treasury strategy also includes active management of preferred claims, making both sides of the November 16 announcement essential to understanding the business.

Reporting sources: Strategy November 16 investor release · The Block figures and context
